name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=tile). '24x24' is the sprite dimension (semantic, not an address residue); 'with_remap_table' describes applying a 256-entry palette LUT (out = remap_table[src_pixel]). No Ghidra address suffix. Name accurately reflects the function's purpose and is convention-compliant. It is documented thoroughly to distinguish from the near-identical sibling fd2_tile_blit_24x24_remap @ 0x4DCC6 (whose 0xC0..0xFF branch remaps existing dst pixels in place, vs the TRUE transparent skip here), so the keep verdict stands.
purpose: Hand-written RLE blit of a 24x24 sprite into a destination buffer, mapping every painted pixel through a 256-entry palette translation table; the 0xC0..0xFF command is a TRUE transparent skip (background passes through unchanged).
logic_summary: Decodes a 24x24-tile RLE stream one command byte at a time over 24 rows, x_remain starting at 0x18 per row. Top two bits of the command select the mode, low 6 bits + 1 = run length: 00 RUN (paint len pixels of remap_table[one src byte] contiguously); 01 STRIDE-2 RUN (same single remapped pixel, written every other dst byte via INC EDI; STOSB, dst +2 per pixel); 10 LITERAL (copy len remapped src bytes, one dst each); 11 TRANSPARENT SKIP (advance dst by len, touching nothing -- no src bytes consumed). At row end dst advances by stride - 0x18 to the next row start. The single difference from the sibling fd2_tile_blit_24x24_remap @ 0x4DCC6 is the 11 branch (skip here vs in-place dst remap there).
signature: void fd2_tile_blit_24x24_with_remap_table(uint32 src, uint32 dst, uint32 stride, uint32 remap_table)

params.name: src
params.semantics: Source RLE-encoded 24x24 sprite stream (linear address). Sole caller passes a per-tile sprite pointer resolved from the battle scene snapshot atlas.
params.reason: Accurate, address-free, matches sibling blitter naming.

params.name: dst
params.semantics: Destination base linear address (battle render workspace position computed by the caller).
params.reason: Accurate, address-free, matches sibling blitter naming.

params.name: stride
params.semantics: Destination row stride in bytes; sole caller passes 0x1C8. The per-row reset advances dst by stride - 0x18.
params.reason: Accurate, address-free, matches sibling blitter naming.

params.name: remap_table
params.semantics: 256-entry palette translation table (linear address); each painted pixel becomes remap_table[src_pixel]. Caller selects a per-chapter anim palette table for cursor-overlay/range-indicator tiles.
params.reason: Accurate, address-free, describes the LUT role precisely.

returns.semantics: No return value; writes pixels directly into the destination buffer.

comment_original_issue: Comment body was already accurate, precise, and correctly distinguished from the sibling fd2_tile_blit_24x24_remap; the only defect was 4 em-dash (U+2014) characters in the Args param block, violating the code-ASCII-only rule.
notes: Sole caller fd2_blit_animated_tile_at_pos @ 0x12AC6 (xref CALL at 0x12C00) blits cursor-overlay / range-indicator battle tiles where the cursor-overlay flag (tile_meta+7) != 0xFF, using a per-chapter anim palette table and stride 0x1C8; the TRUE transparent-skip branch is what lets the underlying map show through tinted overlays. Ghidra plate already comprehensive and consistent with src understanding (it uses em-dashes, but plate text is not bound by the src ASCII rule and does not contradict the refined comment), so left unchanged per the conservative plate rule. No logic touched; only fixed em-dash -> -- in the src comment param block. git add -A had also staged unrelated pre-existing shard changes from sibling runs (0004dcc6.json, 00035c23.json, etc.) and a CRLF-normalization warning; commit scope was restricted to only src/gfx/blittile.c and this shard via explicit per-path staging.
